subject.title: [Bug]: Telegram group: cross-agent sessions_list visibility mismatch causes one-way sessions_send failure

question: Should OpenClaw make same-Telegram-group cross-agent sessions visible/sendable symmetrically under the current session visibility model, or keep them blocked until a per-capability/per-agent authorization contract is approved?
rationale: The likely fix changes the cross-agent session authorization boundary and could expose session metadata or transcript-adjacent state, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security contract.

options.title: Choose the broader authorization contract first
options.body: Keep this issue open, use the related per-capability and per-agent authorization threads to settle semantics, then implement the Telegram proof case against that contract.

options.title: Approve a narrow send-only exception
options.body: Allow `sessions_send` to rely on A2A policy while list/history/status stay visibility-gated, but require live Telegram A/B proof and regression tests before landing.

options.title: Treat current behavior as expected configuration
options.body: Close only if maintainers decide same group membership must not imply cross-agent access and reporters should use the documented `visibility=all` plus A2A path.

recommendation.title: Choose the broader authorization contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open, use the related per-capability and per-agent authorization threads to settle semantics, then implement the Telegram proof case against that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: Their history is closest to the current session-tool security scoping and access-helper boundary that would need to change.
